PART I

Item 1. Business

Our company designs and manufactures advanced semiconductors used in data centers, gaming, and professional visualization. We operate globally, with major engineering sites across North America, Europe, and Asia. Our GPUs power training and inference workloads for the largest AI platforms in the world.

We generate revenue through direct sales to cloud service providers, OEMs, and system integrators. In the most recent fiscal year the data center segment represented the majority of our total revenue, driven by sustained demand for accelerated computing in generative AI workloads.

Our principal competitors include integrated device manufacturers, fabless semiconductor firms, and increasingly, in-house silicon programs operated by hyperscale cloud providers. We compete on performance per watt, developer ecosystem, and total cost of ownership.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties. Our operating results and the market price of our common stock could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks.

Export controls imposed by the U.S. government restrict our ability to sell certain products into specific geographies, including the People's Republic of China. These controls have had, and may continue to have, a material impact on our revenue and may require us to develop region-specific product variants.

Concentration of supply. We rely on a limited number of foundries, chiefly located in Taiwan, for the manufacture of our most advanced products. Any disruption to those foundries, including geopolitical disruption, natural disaster, or capacity constraints, could materially impair our ability to deliver products.

Item 2. Properties

Our principal corporate offices are located in Santa Clara, California. We also lease engineering and administrative facilities in North America, Europe, and Asia. We believe our existing facilities are adequate for our current and foreseeable needs.

Item 3. Legal Proceedings

From time to time we are party to various legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business. We do not currently believe that the ultimate outcome of any of these matters will have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis

Revenue for fiscal year 2025 increased substantially year over year, driven by growth in the data center segment. Gross margin expanded as the product mix shifted toward higher-value compute platforms. Operating expenses grew in line with headcount investments in research and development.

We continue to invest aggressively in next-generation accelerated computing platforms. We expect research and development expense to grow modestly in the coming fiscal year as we scale product programs across multiple architectures and software stacks.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

We are exposed to market risk primarily related to foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. Our international operations expose us to currency movements between the U.S. dollar and local currencies of the markets in which we operate.
